title.narrative: Restoring Education, Needed Environment and WASH (RENEW)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe RENEW project is a targeted and integrated WASH and Education (EDU) intervention to save lives, stimulate resilience and support sustainable transitions for affected communities including displaced populations, vulnerable host communities, and returnees in areas facing the most severe needs. The activities will provide approximately 16,600 households (83,000 individuals including 23,240 women, 23,240 men, 18,260 girls, and 18,260 boys) with WASH and EDU assistance in Rural Damascus, Homs, and Latakia. This will include the rehabilitation of 3 schools, non-formal education (NFE) services to 1,200 vulnerable children, and WASH rehabilitations to 5 vulnerable communities (83,000 individuals). All education beneficiaries will also benefit from WASH interventions. ltbrgtProject locations include Babella, Rural Damascus (Hseniyeh and Sbeineh) for 50,000 individuals, Al Qusayr, Homs (Arjoun and Dabaa) for 8,000 individuals and Mazar Al Qatarieh in Hanadi, Lattakia for 25,000 individuals. ltbrgtThis project is designed to support Standard Allocation Envelope 1, humanitarian support to displaced populations and vulnerable host communities (Babella - 53% of the budget) and Envelope 2, supporting safe and dignified return from areas of displacement to areas of origin (Al Qusayr and Hanadi - 47% of the budget). The project all levels of society by enhancing individual (improved education level, ability to obtain and maintain employment), household (increased water access better prospects for supporting one’s family through work following education), and community level resilience (improved water systems leading to improve health, less reliance on negative coping mechanisms reduced number of out of school children (OOSC) contributes to reductions in unemployment, early marriage, future homelessness risk, etc., with compounding positive community effects). ltbrgtThe project’s design was based on a general needs assessment, market assessment and household level assessment from potential beneficiaries which verified the urgent need for assistance, the suitability of the planned intervention (WASH and EDU) and the appropriateness (present sites for rehabilitation presence of OOSC, etc.), ensuring the protection especially of women, girls and PwD and the environment. Before implementation, ADRA will hold community engagement meetings to explain the project's objectives, duration, expected impact, expected behavior of ADRA staff and information on the complaint mechanisms, and conduct rigorous monitoring of all project activities. ltbrgtADRA has extensive experience implementing WASH and EiE projects across Syria, including in most planned locations. ADRA maintains a head office in Damascus serving Rural Damascus, and field offices in both Lattakia and Homs with an assigned area manager, staff and daily workers. ADRA likewise has full access to all where this project targets, and has existing agreements with authorities that simplify and expedite the approval process for activities. This project will be implemented in tandem with existing activities in the targeted governorates, and will likewise be coordinated with other actors in the locations, incl. HAC and relevant line ministries. ADRA has already communicated with other organizations (such as INGOs / NNGOs) to ensure that planned activities compliment, rather than duplicate other interventions.ltbrgtMaximizing humanitarian value at cost is a priority of this intervention. Direct activity inputs have been prioritized comprising of 81% of the total budget (section B Supplies and D Contractual Services), representing a cost-efficient operation in line with SHF standards. The cost / beneficiary for the WASH interventions is estimated at slightly higher than the average as envelope 2 is targeting areas of return, and the number of beneficiaries is likely to increase by the end of the project. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe RENEW project is linked with ADRA Syria HRP projects #HSYR24-EDU-212174-1 and HSYR24-WSH-212692-1. lt/pgt
